newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish grain, rapeseed imports duty-free to mid-97.
newsitem.headline: Polish grain, rapeseed imports duty-free to mid-97.

text.p: The Polish government has decided to keep grain and rapeseed imports duty-free until the end of June 1997, a deputy agriculture minister said on Tuesday.
"The council of ministers has decided to extend the suspension of import duties on grain and rapeseed until the end of June 1997," Jerzy Pilarczyk told a news briefing after a cabinet meeting.

With domestic consumption estimated at about 25.2 million tonnes and production at about 24 million, Poland's import needs are estimated at between 1.3 and 1.7 million tonnes in the 1996/97 growing season (July/June).
The country bought 1.8 million tonnes abroad in 1995/96. The imports would include high gluten wheat, which is not grown in Poland.
Pilarczyk also said that Poland's food market regulator, the state-run Agriculture Market Agency (ARR), would have to buy abroad the grain it needed to rebuild its reserves.
"We do not want grain purchases by the ARR to create additional demand on the domestic market," Pilarczyk said.

Poland's 1996 rapeseed output is estimated at 438,000 tonnes, down from 1.38 million last year. According to the agriculture ministry Poland has already imported some 127,500 tonnes of rapeseed since this year's harvest.
